papers.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
papers.abs: GUI web agents require realistic and interactive environments that remain stable during both evaluation and training. Live website evaluation suffers from changing content, access restrictions, and limited coverage of authenticated workflows, while existing synthetic environments for training often lack functional depth and visual fidelity. We propose WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable and dockerized website environments that faithfully reconstruct the visual interfaces, content, and functional workflows of real-world web services under deterministic control. We build WebHarbor through task-driven human-agent collaboration, where environments evolve as new tasks expand their functional scope, coding agents implement the required changes, and human contributors audit visual fidelity, functional correctness, and task validity. The resulting suite comprises 3,518 tasks spanning multi-step and post-authentication workflows, where existing works often fail to cover. Beyond reliable evaluation, WebHarbor provides high-fidelity synthetic web environments for cost-efficient reinforcement learning (RL). We demonstrate that a Qwen 4B-level GUI agent trained with RL in WebHarbor generalizes to unseen tasks and performs competitively with leading open-source GUI web agents across four benchmarks. The code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/aiming-lab/WebHarbor.
papers.ko: 웹하버: 진화하는 GUI 에이전트 환경을 위해 실제 웹 사이트를 닷킹

papers.title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
papers.abs: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation has substantially improved the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, including code generation, data analysis, and exam-style question answering. Despite these advances, purely neural LLMs continue to struggle with elementary logical reasoning problems and lack the determinism, soundness, and reliability characteristic of symbolic reasoning systems. Conversely, classical symbolic methods such as SAT solving and exact cover guarantee correctness and completeness, but require problems to be expressed in highly specialized formal encodings, limiting their applicability to natural language inputs. In this work, we present a synergistic neuro-symbolic framework that bridges this gap by combining neural semantic parsing with deterministic exact cover reasoning. Given a Zebra-style logic puzzle in natural language, an LLM translates entities and constraints into structured tool calls that construct an exact cover instance. A symbolic solver then computes the solution and provides feedback to iteratively refine invalid, under- or overconstrained encodings, exploiting the uniqueness property of Zebra puzzles. We conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple parameter scales, post-training paradigms, and LLM families. The results demonstrate that our hybrid approach consistently outperforms strong plain neural baselines, including CoT prompting, as well as recent neuro-symbolic methods.
papers.ko: 자연어 에서 정확한 표지판: 제브라 퍼즐 에 대한 신경 상징적 인 접근법

papers.title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
papers.abs: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.
papers.ko: 에고 액션 벤치: 에고센트릭 인적 비디오에 대한 밀집한 액션 캡션 벤치마크

papers.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
papers.abs: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment. Finally, because estimated actions cannot fully capture contact-rich interactions, we collect on-policy human corrections through DAgger to improve performance. We evaluate Pixel-UMI on five challenging tasks spanning articulated-object manipulation, deformable-object handling, constrained-space reaching, whole-body collision avoidance, and contact-rich bimanual coordination, achieving 87.0% average task progress. Video results are available at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel-umi
papers.ko: 픽셀-UMI: 학습 환경 인식 센서화된 인간 시위로부터 온몸 조작

papers.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
papers.abs: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel
papers.ko: 픽셀: 일반목적 모바일 조작을 배울 수 있는 공동 설계된 풀 스택 로봇 시스템

papers.title: Total Cost of Agency: Exact Attribution of Memory Injection Cost in Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
papers.abs: Every node in a multi-agent large language model (LLM) workflow retrieves context from memory and injects it into its prompt, where those injected tokens are billed as input tokens at the same per-token price as the system prompt and the user query. Production observability tools report total token cost but do not separate the tokens a node generates from the tokens it is handed, so this component of the bill is invisible to the teams paying it. We introduce the Total Cost of Agency (TCA), a decomposition of multi-agent workflow cost into base prompt, inference, memory injection, miss penalty and context-accumulation components, and an exact attribution method: a two-pass, non-billable token count that measures injected tokens directly rather than estimating them from word-count proxies. On a 200-task enterprise benchmark executed against real model APIs, memory injection accounts for 13.6 percent of the variable cost a compile-time optimizer can act on, about 12 percent of the full billed cost, and its share rises from a structural zero at workflow depth one to 27.6 percent at depth six. Injected tokens grow linearly with depth over the measured range (R^2 = 0.9974, depths two through six); a quadratic fit yields a negative leading coefficient, so the data do not exhibit convex growth at these depths. We show the component is controllable at fixed model tier: reducing the retrieval window capacity from 32 to 2 entries lowers injected tokens by 28.7 percent with an accuracy change within seed-level variation. We report in full that our graph-rewriting transforms are approximately cost-neutral in isolation, that two of the five decomposition terms are zero by construction in this harness, and that total workflow cost is dominated by model tier assignment, which we hold fixed and treat as prior work. Prompt caching is not evaluated; all figures are for the uncached case.
papers.ko: 에이전트 전체 비용: 멀티 에이전트 LLM 작업 흐름에서 메모리 주입 비용의 정확한 배분

papers.title: Anchored Fusion for Automated Airway Segmentation in Pediatric and Adult CT
papers.abs: Airway segmentation from chest CT enables branch-level measurement of airway size and growth, but peripheral bronchi remain hard to segment, particularly in children, whose airways are smaller and for whom few annotated scans exist. Different models recover complementary branches of the airway tree. Their union improves overall tree coverage but also introduces disconnected non-airway objects. We propose anchored fusion (A-Fuse), which takes the voxel-wise union of TfeNet, a retrained MEDPSeg and a reimplemented AirMorph and retains the connected component with greatest overlap with the AirMorph mask. On 30 held-out adult CTs from the ATM'26 training set, A-Fuse reaches a Dice score of 93.24% and the highest branch detection rate among compared methods (92.05%). On nine pediatric scans, it reaches 94.15% Dice and 68.79% branch detection. A-Fuse retains the airway tree in all 39 test scans, whereas keeping the largest component selects a non-airway object in four. A-Fuse is deployed as an automated web application and we release all code, trained weights and an open-source ITK-SNAP extension for 3D tubular segmentation editing.

papers.title: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning
papers.abs: Atmospheric fronts are associated with much of the high-impact weather in the mid-latitudes, yet their identification and classification remain largely manual and subjective. Existing deep learning approaches rely primarily on gridded reanalysis or forecast data, limiting their applicability to satellite observations available for time-critical applications. We introduce SATFRONT, a machine learning framework for detecting cold, warm, and occluded fronts over Europe from geostationary satellite observations, with reanalysis data as an optional additional input. The model is trained on frontal analyses from five European national meteorological services and evaluated against UK Met Office analyses for 2024. Using satellite observations alone, SATFRONT achieves a Critical Success Index (CSI) of 0.428 at a 150 km tolerance, within the range of agreement between analyses from different meteorological services (0.277-0.501) and higher than that of an operational rule-based front detector that uses satellite data (0.133). Adding ERA5 reanalysis increases the CSI to 0.591. ERA5 substantially improves the placement of individual fronts, although its effect on their annual spatial distribution varies by front type. These results demonstrate that cold, warm, and occluded fronts can be detected directly from geostationary satellite observations, providing a basis for automated frontal analyses at the high temporal frequency required for time-critical applications.
papers.ko: SATFRONT: 기계 학습을 사용하여 위성 데이터로 대기 전선을 탐지

papers.title: InSARFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Interferometric SAR
papers.abs: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables the analysis of topological changes in natural sites or urban areas. This technique operates by recovering the surface displacement from the study of the phase difference (interferogram) between two or multiple SAR images of the same scene at different times. In practice, the use of phase denoising algorithms is necessary to extract relevant information from the interferograms, which motivated numerous developments in the past decade. Due to the inherent periodicity of phases, interferograms can naturally be represented as points on a Riemannian manifold (specifically, the flat torus). This strong prior knowledge motivates the design of learning-based methods that respect the interferogram's intrinsic geometric constraints. Building on this observation, this paper introduces InSARFlow: a generative modeling framework for the denoising and generation of interferograms. Unlike conventional deep learning approaches formulated in Euclidean spaces, which may violate phase periodicity and produce invalid estimates, this method leverages Riemannian flow matching to learn distributional transports directly on the torus. The interest of this approach is demonstrated on two use cases: (1) realistic interferogram generation, in which we model the transport between uniform noise on the torus to real-world interferograms; (2) interferogram denoising, where InSARFlow transports noisy interferograms to their denoised counterparts. Extensive experiments on a controlled synthetic dataset validate the effectiveness of InSARFlow for interferogram denoising. The proposed approach consistently outperforms studied baselines, highlighting the benefits of geometry-aware learning on the torus. Code and weights available at https://github.com/lebellig/insarflow.
papers.ko: INSARFlow: 인터페로메트릭 SAR에 대한 리만니언 흐름 일치

papers.title: Do the Numbers Match the Plot? Statistical-Visual Verification for Automated Exploratory Data Analysis
papers.abs: Automated exploratory data analysis (EDA) systems can execute statistics correctly while producing misleading interpretations. For example, correlations may be driven by influential observations, and mean differences may arise from skewness, overlap, or sparse subgroups rather than broad distributional shifts. We present EDAgent, a sequential framework that performs targeted visual verification before report synthesis. For each finding, the system records the statistical result, generates a visualization request identifying relevant distributional features, creates the corresponding chart, and uses the observed pattern to retain, qualify, or reconsider the interpretation. We call this process statistical-visual verification. EDAgent includes VisPlan, an 8B-parameter model that converts visualization rationales into detailed chart plans. We evaluate 87 end-to-end reports on EDA-Bench using a six-dimension rubric and GPT-5.1 multimodal evaluation. Maximum-score proportions reached 87.4% for factuality and visual consistency, 93.1% for statistical-visual cross-validation, and 96.6% for analytical narrative. On 166 open-ended VisEval tasks, VisPlan improved the mean overall score from 4.55 (Qwen3-8B) to 4.62, with the largest gain in aesthetics. These descriptive results indicate that visual verification can make automated EDA reports more transparent about how statistical findings relate to underlying data structure.
papers.ko: 숫자 는 음모 와 일치 합니까? 자동화된 탐구 데이터 분석을 위한 통계-비주얼 검증

papers.title: Cultural Evolution Drives the Emergence of Conventions in Neural Emergent Communication
papers.abs: Recent studies of language evolution with neural agents often use models where agents can either speak or listen, where there are only two agents in the population, or where agents can share internal representations. These choices prevent the study of how language emerges through cultural evolution, i.e. through the cumulative adaptation of individual behaviours to fit the communicative needs of the community. We tackle this issue with a new model that trains populations of bi-directional neural agents in a fully distributed fashion to solve a referential game. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on multiple image datasets and show that it is able to scale to large populations. We also show that more conventional languages are easier to learn, providing a direct advantage for cultural transmission. Overall, this work provides a novel approach to neural emergent communication that opens up new directions for evolutionary linguistics.
