papers.title: J-Anchor: Defending Against Prefill Attacks via J-Space Selective Refusal Restoration
papers.abs: Prefill jailbreaks can cause safety-aligned language models to continue an unsafe assistant prefix even when they would refuse the same request under normal decoding. We study how the model's internal harmfulness and refusal signals evolve along this attacker-controlled trajectory. Using the Jacobian lens, we track vocabulary-grounded harmfulness and refusal signals from the assistant header through prefilling and subsequent generation. We identify a characteristic phenomenon, which we call refusal-state erosion: both the refusal signal and the harmfulness signal weaken as the prefill progresses, but the refusal signal progressively declines to the benign baseline by the end of the prefill, while the harmfulness signal remains above its benign baseline and detectable during subsequent generation. Motivated by this observation, we introduce J-Anchor, a training-free inference-time defense that uses the model's pre-attack harmfulness and refusal signals as a request-specific anchor and selectively restores weakened refusal in J-space during prefilling and decoding. J-Anchor substantially reduces attack success under both fixed and deep prefill attacks across different model families. J-Anchor largely preserves benign behavior and reasoning ability, and ablations highlight the importance of targeted restoration in the J-space refusal subspace. Our results suggest that preserving latent refusal dynamics offers a promising route to robust defense against prefill jailbreaks.
papers.ko: J-Anchor: J-Space 선택적 거부 복구를 통해 사전충전 공격에 대한 방어

papers.title: Infinite Quantiles Inference under Local Differential Privacy
papers.abs: We study simultaneous quantile inference under local differential privacy for a number of target probabilities that grows with the sample size. Each user participates once, so learning unknown quantile locations and calibrating their joint uncertainty must share the same private information. We fuse complementary cumulative distribution function (CDF) scores from a single tree report using their exact covariance; the variance at the correct anchor is no larger than that of either score, and anchor error incurs only quadratic excess variance. Three consecutive cohorts then localize the quantiles, estimate their densities, and supply fresh scores for a one-step correction and joint multiplier calibration. Under mild conditions, a uniform representation controls localization and density errors and yields asymptotically valid simultaneous coverage. A fixed-privacy regime permits every polynomially growing target grid. Simulations show consistent same-report precision gains, while comparisons with CDF-band inversion expose the sample cost of learning target locations. Census microdata illustrates how the resulting joint intervals support wage-percentile ratios.

papers.title: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
papers.abs: The kernel of the Lean proof assistant checks that a proof establishes its statement. Whether the statement says what was intended is left to human reviewers. This is the old problem of validating a specification, and it grows more pressing as language models write formal statements in bulk and agents edit formal developments continuously. We present ProofPatch, a tool that helps reviewers judge Lean statements and keeps their judgments valid while the development changes. A reviewer can ask the kernel targeted questions about a statement, such as whether a hypothesis is needed or whether a counterexample exists. Each decision is stored with fingerprints of the statement as Lean elaborated it and of the definitions it depends on, and any declaration can be pinned so that a patch changing it is blocked, whether a person or an agent built on a large language model (LLM) wrote the patch. Working on elaborated terms rather than source text is the central design choice: notation and formatting changes leave a decision intact, and a changed definition reaches every theorem that uses it. On 229 pairs of consecutive revisions of Mathlib, Lean's mathematics library, ProofPatch sends 118 of 12,898 synthetic decisions back for review. Every text-based alternative misses at least 38 of these or sends back at least 13 times as many. On 1,527 labeled statements, kernel evidence flags unfaithful ones with precision 0.88 to 0.96, and in 344 runs of an LLM agent no change to a pinned statement got through.
papers.ko: 증명 패치: 린 진술을 검토하고 공식화가 발전함에 따라 리뷰를 유효하게 유지합니다

papers.title: Benign population landscapes do not transfer to empirical risk minimization in nonsmooth optimization
papers.abs: Benign landscapes provide a geometric explanation for the success of iterative methods on nonconvex problems arising in data science. The landscape is benign if every local minimizer is global and every other critical point is a strict saddle. For methods that avoid strict saddles, convergence to a critical point therefore implies convergence to a global minimizer. For smooth stochastic optimization, a common strategy for establishing such landscapes proceeds in two steps: $(i)$ establish benign geometry for the population objective---which is often easier to analyze---and $(ii)$ transfer this geometry to the empirical objective using concentration of gradients and Hessians. Recent work has extended saddle-point avoidance guarantees to weakly convex nonsmooth optimization through the notion of active strict saddles. We show, however, that benign population geometry need not transfer to empirical objectives in this setting. Specifically, for robust phase retrieval with Gaussian measurements---a well-studied and highly structured problem---the population objective is benign. Nevertheless, the empirical objective has sharp spurious local minima with probability bounded away from zero as the sample size tends to infinity. This asymptotic probability lower bound is independent of the dimension.
papers.ko: 양성 인구 풍경은 비무끄러운 최적화에서 경험적 위험 최소화로 전환되지 않습니다

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Minimax Prediction for Stationary Renewal Processes
papers.abs: The minimax next-symbol Kullback-Leibler risk for stationary binary renewal processes is known to have order n^(-1/2). We give a polynomial-time predictor attaining this order for an arbitrary unknown finite-mean interarrival law. The construction uses a classical type-uniform renewal code. Its contribution is an exact dynamic program for censored prefix marginals, avoiding enumeration of gap histograms or binary completions. Combined with an established prediction reduction, it gives risk at most [log M_(n+1)+log(n+2)]/n, where M_N counts renewal types. Shared suffix updates reduce the total computation to O(n^3) arithmetic work and polynomial bit complexity, without tail, mixing, known-mean, or bounded-support assumptions. The statistical rate and its lower bound are prior results; the proposed advance concerns computation.
papers.ko: 정지적인 재생 과정에 대한 다항식 시간 최소 예측

papers.title: CipherFlow: Compiling AI Programs for Efficient Cryptographically Secure Inference
papers.abs: Cryptographically secure inference faces two practical challenges: making secure programming accessible to AI developers and data scientists, and achieving efficient execution across deployment environments. Developers must compose cryptographic primitives correctly, while performance depends on hardware, networks, and evolving ciphertext states. We present CipherFlow, a compiler framework that takes a high-level AI computation graph, available cryptographic primitives, and a target hardware and network configuration to generate an executable, latency-optimized secure inference program. CipherFlow automates cryptographic execution decisions through three techniques: MicroBench profiles deployment-specific primitive costs; state-expanded planning jointly optimizes homomorphic encryption (HE) and secure multi-party computation (MPC) placement, conversions, and ciphertext maintenance under cryptographic-state constraints; and BlockFold summarizes branched regions to scale planning to Transformer graphs. Evaluation using measured HE/MPC backend costs across CPU/GPU and network settings shows up to 16.5$\times$ speedup on BERT-base and over 22$\times$ on ViT compared with static hybrid placement baselines. CipherFlow separates model programming from cryptographic execution decisions, enabling developers to express AI computations while the compiler constructs efficient secure programs.
papers.ko: 시퍼플로우: 효율적인 암호화 보안 인퍼런스를 위한 인공지능 프로그램을 컴파일

papers.title: An auditable agentic pipeline for variant-to-gene prioritisation, validated against orthogonal functional evidence
papers.abs: Assigning GWAS variants to causal genes requires evidence from multiple resources. We present V2G, an agentic pipeline that records evidence retrieval and returns ranked genes alongside the retrieved evidence. We evaluate whether language-model reranking improves gene prioritisation and whether its gains depend on the retrieved evidence or recall of known associations. On 135 held-out loci where candidate retrieval succeeded and Open Targets L2G predicts, reranking by a language model improves Precision@1 over the evidence ordering it receives, 0.793 against 0.711 (+0.081, 95% CI +0.038 to +0.129), and over nearest-gene assignment (+0.178); no difference from Open Targets L2G or from training-membership baselines was detected. Given only the trait and the candidate gene symbols, in shuffled order, the same model scores 0.864 on these loci (three seeds, 0.859 - 0.867) and names the reference gene at 0.594 of the loci where the pipeline never retrieved it; with each gene's symbol moved to another gene's evidence row it follows the top-scored row and scores 0.284. The gain over the evidence ordering is recall of known genes, and the evidence as presented anchors the model to the ordering rather than informing it. Across the 296 held-out loci (five seeds each) the model keeps the given top candidate at 86% of decisions; at naturally retrieved loci its departures select a reference gene in 85% of departure decisions (31 of 37 loci), and none displaced one. Its calls carry trait-matched mouse mutant or Mendelian phenotype annotations more often than other candidates at the same locus. Train-test overlap is reported throughout. The study includes a frozen benchmark, cached predictions and reproduction code.
papers.ko: 변종에서 유전자에 대한 우선순위를 결정하기 위한 검증 가능한 에이전틱 파이프라인, 정렬 기능적 증거에 의해 검증된

papers.title: DIMWIT: Directly Invoking Models Without Intensive Tuning
papers.abs: Resource managers typically encode what to do in a task-specific policy---a heuristic, an optimization procedure, or a model trained for the task---that must be developed before use and may need revision as the workload or system changes. We propose bypassing policy development and instead asking pretrained models to make resource-management decisions directly, given the current system state, desired outcome, and available choices. We evaluate this approach on microservice autoscaling, DRAM sizing, and video encoding, using a frontier LLM and two small decision models. On two microservice applications, a small decision model meets latency targets while using within 10% of the replicas allocated by policy-based autoscalers and within 13% of the frontier LLM. In DRAM sizing, a small decision model reduces DRAM usage by up to 27.5% relative to static provisioning while maintaining at least 95% of baseline performance. In video encoding, it completes encodes up to 4.3$\times$ faster than the frontier LLM, with an imperceptible 1.1-point decrease in Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), a metric of perceptual video quality. Making individual resource-management decisions may be considerably simpler than developing a general strategy for making them.
papers.ko: DIMWIT: 집중적인 조율 없이 직접 모형을 불러오는 것

papers.title: A Surrogate Model for Variation-Aware Clock-Mesh Analysis and Design-Space Exploration using Graph Neural Networks
papers.abs: Clock meshes are widely used in high-performance VLSI systems to minimize skew and tolerate On-Chip Variation (OCV) in nanometer technologies. However, analyzing meshes is difficult because reconvergent paths and multi-source drivers prevent static timing analysis (STA) tools from handling mesh loops, making SPICE the industrial standard. SPICE simulations are accurate but slow, so clock-mesh synthesis relies on approximate models that overlook critical effects such as non-linear buffer driving caused by input slew and input skew. We propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based surrogate model of the clock mesh with a new graph representation and a new architecture that predicts power while also improving the delay and slew predictions at the sinks and capturing the skew histogram under OCV. Trained on SPICE data and tested on unseen real designs, our model achieves average errors of $3.40$~ps in delay, $4.14$~ps in slew and $4.46$~ps in skew, compared with $6.28$~ps, $12.35$~ps, and $11.62$~ps for our prior model, and $74.37$~ps delay and $27.51$~ps skew for the approximate method used in current state-of-the-art works. Our model predicts power within $3.4\%$ of SPICE on average, while delivering $18\times$-$1706\times$ speed-ups over the approximate method under OCV modeling, enabling faster and more accurate clock-mesh design-space exploration. A case study on a real design further shows that our surrogate model finds buffering candidates that, at a balanced tradeoff, improves $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile skew by $49.1\%$, reduces power by $25.7\%$, and reduces area by $37.3\%$ at the cost of a $6.8\%$ increase in $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile maximum slew as compared to the state-of-the-art work.
papers.ko: 그래프 신경망을 이용한 변형 인식 시계-망 분석 및 설계 공간 탐구의 대리 모델

papers.title: Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer for Joint Multipath Parameter Estimation: Applications to mmWave Positioning and Radio SLAM
papers.abs: Future 6G wireless networks are expected to evolve toward AI-native systems that support intelligent, environment-aware services, including positioning and mapping. Current research has already integrated AI into several aspects of communication, particularly wireless channel estimation. However, most learning-based channel estimators focus on communication-oriented objectives rather than explicitly estimating multipath parameters such as delay, angle of arrival (AoA), and angle of departure (AoD). These parameters provide essential geometric information for downstream tasks including positioning and radio simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). In this work, we propose a Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer (SCFT) for joint multipath component (MPC) estimation from noisy complex channel estimates and physical beam-pair descriptors. SCFT combines local spectral convolution, permutation-equivariant beam-set attention, and a query-based Transformer decoder to detect and classify line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths and estimate their observed delays, AoAs, and AoDs. Experiments on realistic ray-tracing data show that SCFT reduces the generalized optimal sub-pattern assignment (GOSPA) error by 13.4% compared with ResNet, the strongest competing baseline. We further demonstrate this advantage in independent snapshot positioning and radio SLAM, where SCFT reduces position RMSE by 18.5% and 65.0%, respectively, relative to ResNet. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly recovering multipath geometry, as improvements in MPC estimation can translate into substantial gains in downstream tasks.
papers.ko: 복합 다방향 파라미터 추정: mmWave 위치 및 라디오 SLAM에 적용

papers.title: OpenULF: A Modular Toolkit Enables Data-Driven Ultra-Low-Field MRI with both Classical and Quantum Sensors
papers.abs: Ultra-low-field (ULF) Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) offers a portable, low-cost alternative to conventional scanners by operating at field strengths below 10 mT. At these fields, two sensor technologies compete: quantum SQUID (Superconducting Quantum Interference Device) sensors, which provide high sensitivity but require cryogenic cooling, and classical induction coils, which are inexpensive and room-temperature but produce weaker signals. With conventional physics-based imaging, both suffer from low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). Data-driven reconstruction has overcome similar limits in related inverse problems, but its use for ULF-MRI has been hindered by a lack of open datasets, benchmarks, and flexible simulators. To close this gap, we present OpenULF, a modular, open-source simulation toolkit that generates paired training data and supports end-to-end machine-learning (ML) reconstruction. OpenULF integrates a Bloch-equation-validated physics simulator, calibrated SQUID and coil receiver models, reconstruction ML networks, and an automated design-space exploration engine. Architecturally, a receiver abstract base class, a typed HDF5 contract that decouples physics from learning, and a resumable sweep engine make sensors, models, and datasets independently substitutable. Using OpenULF, we train 774 models across four anatomical datasets and conduct three design-space explorations. The effectiveness of ML reconstruction depends strongly on the dataset and the sensor. We identify a SQUID-to-coil crossover near 450 $\mu$T and demonstrate that sensor hardware and ML model capacity can be traded off during system design. Sensor and reconstruction choices must therefore be co-designed: the best sensor is set by the dataset and field strength, not by SNR.
papers.ko: OpenULF: 모듈형 도구 킷은 클래식 및 양자 센서 모두로 데이터 가동된 초하 필드 MRI를 가능하게 합니다

papers.title: AI-Aided and AI-Oriented Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: A Survey
papers.abs: The evolution from 5G to 6G networks marks a transition toward the "intelligence of everything." While 5G enables enhanced connectivity, 6G aspires to embed intelligence directly into communication infrastructures, creating systems that are adaptive, context aware, and capable of autonomous decision making. Realizing such systems depends on harmonizing three fundamental functions that compete for shared network resources and often pursue conflicting goals: (i) sensing for environmental and contextual information acquisition, (ii) communication for reliable and timely information exchange, and (iii) computation for information processing and decision making. This harmonization necessitates shifting from independent optimization to their joint design as a unified system, a paradigm known as Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation (ISCC). In parallel, AI has emerged both as an enabling tool for ISCC optimization and as a workload whose requirements influence ISCC system design. This survey comprehensively examines ISCC from this dual perspective by distinguishing between AI-aided ISCC, in which learning-based methods support the joint design and optimization of sensing, communication, and computation, and AI-oriented ISCC, in which these functions are jointly configured to support learning, inference, and distributed intelligence. The survey further examines the co-design of AI and ISCC, where AI requirements and ISCC constraints jointly shape system and model decisions. It further provides a comparative synthesis of the resulting design approaches, system architectures, performance metrics, and evaluation practices, relates these developments to application-specific requirements across different domains, and identifies open research problems toward scalable, adaptive, and trustworthy AI-ISCC systems.
papers.ko: 인공지능 지원 및 인공지능 지향 통합 감지, 통신 및 컴퓨팅: 설문 조사

papers.title: Task-driven sparse-view planar X-ray computed tomography for axial metrology
papers.abs: Computational imaging can reduce the acquisition burden when the system is designed around task-relevant information rather than complete image recovery. We investigate this framework for sparse-view planar X-ray tomography (XCT) of layered objects, using measurement of the axial termination gap (ATG) of back-drilled printed-circuit-board (PCB) vias as a representative task. Instead of using 3D reconstruction, the proposed method estimates ATG directly from polychromatic projection data through a physics-based sensitivity model. A gated hierarchical estimator first fits ATG together with radiometric perturbations and selectively introduces global geometry and specimen-warp models only when a reduced chi-squared adequacy test and Bayesian information criterion justify the added degrees of freedom. The same low-dimensional perturbation model is incorporated into marginalized Fisher-information analyses, yielding task-specific conditional and calibration-aware Cram'er-Rao bounds. Numerical experiments show that, under a fixed total photon budget, task-driven metrology changes little over 12-64 views, while reconstruction-driven metrology is strongly view-dependent with much larger errors. The direct estimator also follows the expected photon-limited scaling. These results demonstrate a computational sensing strategy in which XCT acquisition, physical modeling, and inference are evaluated according to the quantitative information required by the task rather than for general-purpose volumetric image fidelity.

papers.title: Detecting Generated-Depth Injection Attacks on RGB-D Place Authentication
papers.abs: Advances in monocular depth estimation (MDE) now let an attacker generate depth from publicly available RGB images and submit forged RGB-D queries. Such attacks break a core assumption of RGB-D place authentication: that depth comes from a sensor. We study a presentation attack detection (PAD) classifier that uses geometric consistency between the enrollment and query views, as a software-layer defense. A three-stage evaluation shows how far this classifier detects software-injected depth, depending on how accurately the attacker knows the camera intrinsics. In the first stage, the attacker has only an estimate of the intrinsics, and the PAD classifier separates forgeries generated by all three MDE models with a validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997-0.999. In the second stage, the attacker obtains the exact intrinsics, and the original PAD classifier falls to near chance (AUC 0.54-0.61); a retrained PAD classifier, however, still has the registration residual between enrollment and query as a cue. In the third stage, an oracle evaluation, in which the evaluator fits warps using the ground-truth 3D geometry, shows that detection falls to near chance only in its strongest case, where every valid query keypoint is given its ground-truth 3D coordinate. Of the detection cues, the reprojection error captures the attacker's misestimate of the intrinsics, whereas the registration residual remains even when the attacker knows the exact intrinsics.

papers.title: Principled Human-AI Collaboration in Agentic Workflows
papers.abs: Organizations adopting AI face the challenge of deciding which outputs can be released without human review while meeting the quality standards of human experts. We develop a statistical framework for delegating tasks between experts and black-box generate-verify workflows, in which AI-generated answers are verified and revised over multiple rounds. Before deployment, human experts evaluate selected outputs, and their judgments are used to calibrate the verifier threshold and number of attempts. Our method selects the policy with the highest estimated automation rate among statistically approved candidates, without modifying the generator or verifier. We establish finite-sample control of the error rate among released outputs, characterize the expert evaluations sufficient to attain a target automation rate, and derive a minimax lower bound establishing rate optimality in the quality margin and required confidence. In a MultiHiertt financial question-answering case study, average held-out automation increases from 2.50% to 24.17% as expert evaluations accumulate, while released-output error rates remain around 1.20%. In contrast, heuristics that release answers after consistently high verifier scores either violate the 5% error tolerance or automate at most 1.30% of tasks. Synthetic experiments further examine these theoretical predictions under controlled settings.

papers.title: Impossible Code, Barely Changed Score: A Replay Study of Judge-Based Evaluation
papers.abs: Language models are often used to judge generated code without running it. A useful evaluation should reveal substantial changes in the answers it scores. We examine this requirement by repeating an earlier evaluation on 421 coding problems, comparing Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct with two versions trained using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). One receives rewards from execution tests (CE-trained), and the other from a strong language-model judge (SLJ-trained). The base model's syntax-failure rate remains stable, but the trained checkpoints produce invalid Python on 63%-67% of attempts. Despite this change, the strong judge's Pass@32 scores fall by only about 3 percentage points, from 96.67% to 93.95% for SLJ-trained. Within the later run, allowing more attempts makes the base and trained checkpoints look increasingly similar under the judge. With 128 attempts per question, the judge accepts at least one SLJ-trained answer on 96.44% of problems, compared with 28.27% under execution tests. We recommend reporting the share of answers that pass Python's syntax check alongside every judge-based score. This check requires no tests or code execution and flags invalid answers that the judge accepts, although it cannot establish functional correctness. Our findings show how a high judge-based score can hide substantial output damage and motivate checking an evaluation's sensitivity to change. Project page and code: https://curiousorbitnotes.github.io/evorobust-replay-audit/

papers.title: When Does Sparse Routing Help? The Geometry of Expert Separation in Mixture of Experts
papers.abs: Sparse mixtures of experts combine multiple prediction models while evaluating only a small subset for each input. Although this architecture reduces computation, how expert separation and routing sparsity jointly govern expert recovery remains an open problem. In this paper, we address this question for location Gaussian mixtures of experts with a fixed number of experts by establishing how expert separation and spatial arrangement determine recovery rates. For dense models, our results reveal that when experts form well-separated clusters, the separation geometry is governed by the size of the largest cluster; without a prescribed cluster structure, this geometry is instead driven by the total number of experts. For sparse models, the separation geometry on retained routing regions is determined by the number of active experts, while the contribution of omitted regions is controlled by their total probability. Consequently, activating fewer experts reduces the separation complexity in these bounds. Furthermore, Top-1 routing yields a particularly striking result: experts can be recovered at a rate independent of the separation quantity. Our technical approach combines polynomial interpolation and Gaussian reproducing-kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) test functions with quantitative restriction inequalities that extend pointwise comparisons to expert functions.

papers.title: Surrogate Losses for Fairness-Aware Classification: Fisher Consistency and Calibration
papers.abs: Fairness-aware classification seeks to balance predictive accuracy and fairness across demographic groups. Although surrogate losses facilitate the optimization of fairness-aware objectives, it remains unclear when minimizing these losses yields optimal decisions under the original fairness-aware risk. This paper investigates the statistical validity of surrogate-based fairness-aware classification under demographic parity and equal opportunity, considering both attribute-blind and attribute-aware settings. We introduce fairness-aware Fisher consistency and characterize it through conditions on the derivatives of the surrogate losses. The characterization shows that consistency depends not only on the individual loss functions but also on their interaction within the fairness-regularized objective. We further establish a calibration inequality that relates the excess fairness-aware risk to the excess surrogate risk, providing a quantitative connection between surrogate optimization and the original classification objective. Numerical experiments illustrate how deviations from the consistency conditions affect fairness-aware excess risk and how the regularization parameter influences the well-posedness of surrogate optimization. An application to consumer credit default prediction demonstrates that appropriately calibrated fairness regularization can substantially reduce demographic disparities while maintaining predictive performance.

papers.title: Sharp Generalization for Nonparametric Regression in Interpolation Space by Shallow Over-Parameterized Neural Networks with Channel Attention
papers.abs: We study nonparametric regression using an over-parameterized two-layer ReLU neural network with fixed covariance-based channel attention, trained by gradient descent with both layers updated simultaneously. The spherical covariates follow an arbitrary fixed non-atomic distribution, and the target function lies in an interpolation space with spectral bias widely studied in the statistical learning literature. We prove that early-stopped training achieves regression risk $\cO(\eps_n^2)$, where $\eps_n$ is the critical population rate of the attention kernel $\Kattn$. Its positive eigenvalues are $\lambda_j^{s'}$, where $\lambda_j$ are those of the ReLU feature covariance kernel $K$ and $s'=2s+3$ for $s\ge1$. Under polynomial eigenvalue decay $\lambda_j\asymp j^{-2\alpha}$ with $\alpha>1/2$, the regression risk bound $\cO(\eps_n^2)$ specializes to the minimax optimal rate $\cO(n^{-2\alpha s'/(2\alpha s'+1)})$. Our analysis is based on two new technical results on the optimization and generalization of the attention network. First, the neural network function after every gradient descent iteration admits a decomposition into a function with bounded Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) norm and a uniformly small residual. Second, local Rademacher complexity converts this decomposition into a regression risk bound. Kernel gradient descent on the same ball attains the same rate, while our theorem gives explicit sufficient width and auxiliary-sample conditions for simultaneous network training. Our analysis is further extended to covariates supported on $\RR^d$ through a novel normalization method. Under a sub-Gaussian covariate distribution, the attention network achieves a nearly optimal regression risk $\cO((\log n)n^{-s'(d+3)/(s'(d+3)+d)})$ without a density assumption.
papers.ko: 채널 주의를 가진 얇은 과다 매개 변수화된 신경망에 의해 인터폴레이션 공간에서의 비변수 회귀에 대한 날카로운 일반화

papers.title: How Much Does Random Rotation Help GPTQ? Sharp Worst-Case Rate Gaps in the High-Rate Regime
papers.abs: GPTQ is Babai's nearest-plane algorithm on the lattice of the Cholesky factor of the layer's input second moment $\Sigma$. In the high-rate, entropy-coded regime it needs $\tfrac12\log_2(\AM/\GM)$ of its Cholesky pivots more bits than WaterSIC, which is within $0.255$ bit of the rate-distortion limit for every $\Sigma$; random rotations close most of this gap in practice, and Ordentlich and Polyanskiy asked for the worst-case gap between rotated GPTQ and WaterSIC. We show that after a Haar rotation the $k$-th pivot converges almost surely, uniformly in $k\ge\delta n$ and over spectra $\nu$ of bounded condition number, to $1/S_\nu(-k/n)$, a classical formula from the theory of Lyapunov exponents, and use it to answer the question. Over spectra with condition number $\kappa$ the worst rotated gap is $\tfrac12\log_2\kappa-\log_2\ln\kappa+\tfrac12-\tfrac1{\ln2}+o(1)$ bits, attained only by two-point spectra, just $\tfrac12\log_2\ln\kappa+O(1)$ bits below the worst case without rotation, so rotation cannot replace waterfilling in general. It nearly can on real layers: rotation cuts the cost of an $\eta$-fraction of outlier eigenvalues of size $\mu$ from about $\eta\mu$ to $\eta^2\mu/2$ to leading order, but cannot remove spectral spread on a logarithmic scale; for non-Gaussian weights it also adds a weight-side rate cost, which we characterize exactly under a standard high-rate assumption. On $96$ Hessians of Qwen3 and Llama-3.1 the rotated gap has median $0.04$ bit and maximum $0.36$ bit, against $2$--$5$ bits in the worst case for the same condition numbers, and the limit matches it to within $0.009$ bit.
papers.ko: 무작위 회전은 GPTQ에 얼마나 도움이 됩니까? 높은 요금제에서 가장 심한 경우 급격한 격차

papers.title: Learned optical compression for single-pixel quantitative phase imaging
papers.abs: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) reveals optical path-length variations in transparent objects but typically relies on spatially resolved intensity measurements. Here we numerically and experimentally demonstrate learned optical compression for single-pixel QPI, jointly optimizing a diffractive encoder and a digital neural decoder to concentrate reconstruction-relevant phase information into a compact measurement vector. A single reconfigurable phase-modulation plane sequentially displays the learned encoding patterns, which are independent of the input object, each yielding one scalar intensity measurement. Operating at a visible wavelength, the experimental system reconstructs quantitative phase images of unknown objects with ~40-fold dimensional compression, using only 2.55% as many intensity measurements as reconstructed pixels. Experimental blind testing on handwritten digits and grating-like phase objects achieves mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.945 and 0.848, respectively. Benchmarking under the same measurement budget demonstrates substantially higher reconstruction fidelity than other encoding strategies, highlighting the advantages of learned optical compression. With the optical encoder fixed, decoder-only neural adaptation enables experimental transfer to previously unseen data distributions, extending the utility of the learned measurement representation. These results establish learned optical compression as a measurement-efficient and reusable framework for QPI, integrating phase-information compression into single-pixel intensity measurements while retaining adaptability to new data. This approach paves the way for low-data-rate phase imaging and sensing, with the potential to extend QPI to spectral regions where high-quality detector arrays are costly or unavailable.
papers.ko: 단일 픽셀 양적 단계 영상을 위한 학습된 광학 압축

papers.title: Phase-wise MLLM Tuning for Multi-framework WebUI Code Generation
papers.abs: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance in translating WebUI screenshots into HTML/CSS. However, when they faced multiple frameworks (React/Vue/Angular), they often suffer from negative transfer that leads to compilation failures. These failures commonly stem from mixing framework specific syntax and violating framework constraints. This paper studies supervised fine-tuning for multi-framework WebUI code generation and proposes a phase-wise MLLM tuning method driven by compatibility and heterogeneity signals across frameworks. We first apply a normalization mapping that preserves each framework's native syntax while suppressing noise from variable naming and literal content. We then estimate cross framework heterogeneity and compatibility offline, and automatically derive training groups and their ordering by maximizing a phased objective. Finally, we perform phase-wise adapter tuning to reduce cross framework interference. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that our proposed method improves both generation quality and compilation success rate compared with baselines.

papers.title: SMART-AIMC: Sensitivity-Aware Mixed ADC Resolution with Fine-Grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing
papers.abs: Analog In-Memory Computing (IMC) is a promising paradigm for accelerating GEMM-based AI workloads by executing computations directly within the memory array in the analog domain. While IMC delivers substantial energy and throughput improvements, it can suffer from significant task accuracy degradation due to analog-to-digital converter (ADC) quantization noise, which occurs at the GEMM output and is thus different from weight/activation quantization, which occurs at the GEMM input. Mixed ADC resolution allows IMC modules to choose between high- and low-resolution ADC modes with different energy costs, offering a compelling accuracy-energy trade-off. However, selecting ADC resolutions across IMC units while respecting hardware granularity constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose SMART-AIMC, a Sensitivity-aware Mixed ADC Resolution framework with fine-grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing. SMART-AIMC correlates the algorithmic task loss to hardware ADC quantization noise in the form of an ADC Channel Sensitivity (ACS) metric. Using this metric, SMART-AIMC systematically, and in a disciplined manner, allocates ADC resources to critical computations. Furthermore, we introduce a sensitivity-based channel reordering scheme that overcomes the hardware granularity constraints with no runtime overhead and approaches the optimal ADC quantization possible for the model. Evaluated across diverse workloads, SMART-AIMC unlocks a superior accuracy-energy Pareto frontier, providing (1) higher task accuracy at matched energy budgets and (2) fine-grained tuning across efficiency targets, from aggressive energy savings to near-digital inference accuracy. At the latter operating point, SMART-AIMC achieves $6.99\times$ higher modeled system-level energy efficiency for linear projections than the INT8 digital baseline with negligible accuracy degradation.

papers.title: Beyond Imputation: Mask-Adaptive Conformal Prediction via Tree Embeddings on General Missing Data Mechanisms
papers.abs: Conformal prediction (CP) provides a distribution-free framework for uncertainty quantification with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees. Yet, missing values introduce distributional heterogeneity, where marginal coverage can hide systematic undercoverage for certain missingness patterns. At the same time, existing methods based on distances or smoothness require a continuous representation of partially observed covariates. Although imputation restores continuity, it obscures the missingness patterns and introduces task-dependent overhead. We develop a new CP framework that is \emph{adaptive to missingness patterns}, without imputing covariates. We rely on data augmentation by feature embedding that accounts for missingness. Our framework represents each input with missing values by a tree embedding together with its raw missingness mask, and then learns a regularized quantile score function. Varying the choices for the penalty function and the augmentation enables us to characterize three practically relevant validity levels: exact coordinate-wise validity, exact validity on observed masks, and approximate missingness-conditional guarantees for general mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR). Experiments on synthetic and real datasets support these guarantees and show that the proposed method reduces miscoverage risk while maintaining informative intervals, especially in non-MCAR settings. These results highlight the practical value of uncertainty quantification that adapts to missingness.
papers.ko: 임투테이션을 넘어: 일반적인 실종 데이터 메커니즘에 대한 나무 임베디션을 통해 마스크-응응응적 합성 예측

papers.title: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
papers.abs: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) tackle challenging tasks by dividing work among agents and coordinating their contributions toward shared objectives. Evaluating these systems therefore requires benchmarks that assess not only task-solving performance but also the ability to handle interdependent work. However, existing benchmarks often emphasize task difficulty without substantial collaboration requirements or evaluate only a limited range of predefined collaboration patterns. In this paper, we introduce MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration through interconnected tasks. Rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols, MAC-Bench embeds collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints. Specifically, we mine reusable collaboration structures from selected benchmark tasks at two levels. Local collaboration patterns capture recurring interactions among subtasks, while global task structures characterize how these interactions contribute to complete workflows. Through coarse-to-fine composition, these structures are recombined into task graphs combining different collaboration requirements. Tasks are instantiated in executable environments with automated verification of partial progress and complete task resolution.
papers.ko: MAC 벤치: 상호 연결된 작업을 통해 다중 에이전트 협력을 벤치마킹

papers.title: CacheWeave: Learning to Recompute for Efficient Position-Independent KV Caching
papers.abs: Position-independent caching reuses chunk KV caches across positions and requests. Independent encoding, however, omits cross-chunk interactions and can degrade accuracy. In our study, neither PIC training nor rule-based recomputation, alone or combined, consistently recovers full-prefill accuracy. Oracle-guided recomputation on PIC-trained models improves accuracy at the same budget, motivating better selection. We present CacheWeave, which adapts the full backbone to PIC, then freezes it and trains a model-native block selector on the adapted model's oracles. The selector uses compact cached chunk features and question hidden states without extracting backbone attention scores. It selects contiguous token blocks aligned with KV blocks to support efficient recomputation and limit copy-on-write amplification. Its runtime, CacheWeave-Serve, supports private and shared KV caches, keeps selection and recomputation on the GPU, and stages sliding-window KV for hybrid attention models. Across three models and four tasks, CacheWeave outperforms CacheBlend and ProphetKV by 7.2 and 3.5 percentage points on average at a 5% recomputation budget, with a mean relative accuracy loss of 1.6% to full prefill. With 32-token blocks, CacheWeave-Serve cuts single-request TTFT by up to 16.1x over full prefill and 1.7x over ProphetKV, and raises SLO goodput under load by up to 7.8x.
papers.ko: 캐시 웨이브: 위치 독립적인 KV 캐시링을 위해 효율적인 재컴퓨팅을 배우는 것

papers.title: Convex Regression at Scale: Geometry-Preserving Constraint Sparsification
papers.abs: Convex regression provides a flexible nonparametric estimation framework while incorporating appropriate shape information. However, its standard least-squares formulation has $O(n^2)$ supporting-hyperplane constraints creating a computational bottleneck as the sample size $n$ increases. We study a $K$-nearest-neighbor (KNN) localized relaxation for convex regression where we for each sample, we only maintain the $K$ nearest hyperplane constraints. Under mild regularity conditions, we establish statistical guarantees for our modified estimator in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. In particular, for $d>4$, the population risk of our modified problem can be shown to have equivalent convergence rates as the original least square convex regression estimator of $\widetilde O(n^{-2/d})$ using neighborhoods sizes (i.e. $K=K_n$) of order $\widetilde O(n^{2(d-1)/(2d-1)})$ for general convex functions and $\widetilde O(n^{(d+1)/(d+2)})$ for strongly convex functions. To corroborate our theory, we implement iterative optimization methods to compare the prediction accuracy of the KNN relaxation with those of the full estimator across synthetic convex benchmarks. Our experiments demonstrate that KNN prediction risk approaches the full-estimator prediction risk at neighborhood sizes matching the theoretical scale.

papers.title: Optimization Frameworks & Learning Algorithms for Discrete-Time Mean Field Games
papers.abs: This monograph introduces discrete-time mean field games with finite state and action spaces, emphasizing optimization formulations and learning algorithms. Starting from Markov decision processes and finite-player stochastic games, it develops the notion of mean field Nash equilibrium, establishes existence and uniqueness results under suitable assumptions, and explains how mean field equilibria yield approximate equilibria in large finite-player games. Building on the linear programming formulation of Markov decision processes, occupation measures and primal-dual formulations connect equilibrium computation with mathematical optimization. The monograph presents fixed-point iterations, fictitious play, online mirror descent, and optimization-based methods, discussing their convergence properties and limitations. Numerical examples illustrate crowd motion, traffic routing, epidemic management, and the computation of multiple equilibria. It combines examples, theoretical results, and implementable algorithms, with bibliographic notes providing connections to the broader literature.

papers.title: Rubric-Based Assessment of Student Reports Using Small Language Models
papers.abs: Language models can analyze and assess student texts using predefined rubrics and deliver structured feedback, reducing instructors' workload. However, existing solutions often rely on external services that are resource-intensive, costly, and raise privacy concerns, making them unsuitable for constrained environments. This study evaluates an automated assessment pipeline with three key aims: design for low-resource environments, privacy, and focus on a novel context in cybersecurity education. The pipeline integrates lightweight language models for textual evaluation and a vision-language model for image interpretation. Responses from 105 students were collected over two semesters of an undergraduate course during a cybersecurity exercise on incident response. Results across different hardware configurations show that small models in low-resource environments can achieve up to 97% accuracy in text-only and up to 94% in rich-text assessments. This rivals or even outperforms a large model while adding the benefits of locally hosted assessment. Our solution can help educators and practitioners who need grading assistance without replacing human oversight, especially in environments where cloud-based solutions may be impractical. This study contributes an open-source, locally deployable AI-assisted scoring pipeline that runs on affordable hardware and can be extended to various types of student reports in computing education. As a result, it makes automated assessment accessible to a broad range of educators and institutions.

papers.title: Learning AI Agents, Market Makers, and Stress in Automated Markets
papers.abs: Automated markets increasingly route order flow from learning trading agents through automated market makers (AMMs). We model trader archetypes as AI agents defined by their reward functions and analyze the feedback they create on a constant-product AMM. Herd-dominated and arbitrage-dominated markets of equal size have identical return distributions and turnover, so no rule based on volatility, value-at-risk, stress frequency, or volume can tell them apart; yet their stress episodes differ in length by a factor unbounded in the feedback-to-noise ratio $\beta/s$. Serial statistics identify the feedback sign from $\Theta((s/\beta)^2\log(1/\delta))$ observations, and this rate is tight. When agents trade together, profit-seeking agents ride herds rather than lean against them, leading to all-or-nothing participation. Spread-earning market makers restore stability but make liquidity fragile, with discontinuous collapse and hysteresis; maker--taker pricing, not a uniform fee, is the effective instrument.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Hierarchical Federated Learning for UAV Swarms Across Heterogeneous Environments
papers.abs: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) enables communication-efficient training in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms, but performance degrades under changing and heterogeneous environments. This paper proposes domain-aware HFL (DA-HFL), integrating mobility-informed clustering, cluster-level aggregation, cloud-based Fisher-weighted merging, a domain-adversarial shared backbone, environment-specific heads, and gated inference with local adaptation. A mission-weighted optimization formulation incorporates energy, latency, and cluster-head eligibility constraints. Theoretical analysis establishes resource feasibility, a conditional backbone-stationarity bound, the quadratic optimality of Fisher-weighted merging, and communication and computation complexity bounds. Simulations across four heterogeneous environments demonstrate faster convergence, improved accuracy during environmental transitions, and more stable, purer clusters than the evaluated baselines, with modest energy overhead over resource-aware HFL. Ablation studies validate the contributions of the proposed components.

papers.title: The Scope Grammar of Natural-Language Rules: Counting and Enumerating Readings modulo Logical Equivalence
papers.abs: A rule written for people fixes its atomic conditions and connectives but leaves open how the connectives are bracketed, and each bracketing is a different logical reading that an autoformalizer must resolve or expose. We study the scope grammar, a deliberately ambiguous context-free grammar whose derivation trees are the readings of a connective skeleton and whose quotient by logical equivalence is what matters downstream. A skeleton with $k$ binary connectives has $C_k$ derivation trees, the $k$-th Catalan number, but far fewer logically distinct readings. For the positive, repetition-free fragment we make the gap exact: through the uniqueness of the read-once normal form we characterize the realizable normal forms by lowest common ancestors and count them with a two-label recurrence over the operator word, verified against exhaustive enumeration up to eleven atoms. The count is invariant under reversal and $\wedge/\vee$ duality; a skeleton is ambiguous if and only if it uses both $\wedge$ and $\vee$, a one-pass test; and the number of classes is at least $2^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$. Up to fifteen atoms the alternating pattern is the worst case; its count has a cubic generating function, is the 3-Schr\"oder sequence (OEIS A137842), and grows with base $\varphi^{5/2}\approx3.330$, below the Catalan base 4. We reduce maximality to an inequality on increments, verified to sixteen atoms, and explain why local exchange arguments cannot prove it. We also treat negation, exceptions, and background axioms, where normal-form uniqueness still decides equivalence but counting is open.

papers.title: MEX: The Musical Expectation Benchmark Suite
papers.abs: We propose the Musical Expectation (MEX) benchmark suite for perceptually validating computational models of musical expectation, i.e., models that estimate music information dynamics (MID) measures of perceived musical expectations, such as surprisal or uncertainty from symbolic music or musical audio. MEX collects and extends tasks for evaluating such models previously proposed in music information retrieval and cognitive sciences using standard datasets, and evaluates whether: (1) proposed MID measures decrease with repetition due to in-context learning of the computational model, (2) peaks in such measures align with boundaries of music segments, (3) pitch surprisal and uncertainty estimated from audio are consistent with those modeled in event-based symbolic music, (4) proposed MID measures can predict electrophysiological responses to music. We stress that this benchmark suite does not provide an exhaustive computational characterization of music expectation. Rather, we envision this as an active, interdisciplinary initiative, with benchmarks evolving as our understanding of the underlying perceptual processes deepens. We provide open-access code https://github.com/musicperceptmodeling/mex to estimate surprisal and uncertainty from audio using baseline models, run the tasks on standard datasets, and include utilities for running the tasks with users' own data.
papers.ko: MEX: 뮤지컬 기대 벤치마크 스위트

papers.title: FADE: A Flow-Based Approach for Multichannel Tail Estimation
papers.abs: Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) is vulnerable to rare low-received-power events, and the spatial-diversity benefits of multiple receivers can be significantly reduced when they experience simultaneous deep fading. Multivariate Extreme Value Theory (MEVT) provides a principled framework for characterizing such joint tail behavior. However, conventional MEVT methods often rely on restrictive parametric assumptions or discrete representations of the dependence structure, which may not fully capture complex multivariate tail behavior. This paper proposes Flow-based Angular Density Estimation (FADE), a flow-based approach for characterizing the dependence between extreme events across receivers within the MEVT framework. FADE transforms multivariate extremes into a standard extreme-value representation and uses a flow-based density estimator to learn the dependence structure from the transformed data without imposing a predefined parametric form. The proposed framework is evaluated using experimentally collected data from a UAV communication system, in which the UAV serves as the transmitter and communicates with two ground receivers. FADE provides closer agreement with the empirical joint CDF, achieving reductions of up to 22.4% in MAE compared with the state-of-the-art Logistic and Maximum Empirical Likelihood (MEL) methods, while also improving distributional agreement and reducing absolute bias.
papers.ko: FADE: 다채널 꼬리 추정에 대한 흐름 기반 접근법

papers.title: Efficient Lempel-Ziv Prediction with the Run-Length BWT
papers.abs: Lempel-Ziv Plurality (LZP) is an algorithm of Kosoy that predicts the next symbol of a string by using its Lempel-Ziv factorization, and makes at most $O(z\log n)$ mistakes on every string of length $n$ with $z$ LZ77 phrases. We give efficient online implementations of LZP and of a new variant of it. Our first implementation maintains a run-length encoded Burrows-Wheeler transform (RLBWT) of the reversed history. It implements LZP, uses $O(z\log z\log^2 n)$ bits, and has worst-case update and prediction times $O(\log z+\log\log n)$ and $O(\sigma(\log z+\log\log n))$, respectively, where $\sigma$ is the size of the alphabet. This is an exponential improvement over Kosoy's implementation, whose update time is $O(z\log^7 n)$. We then introduce the Lempel-Ziv Majority (LZM) predictor, which has the same mistake bound and update time, and predicts in $O(1)$ time independently of $\sigma$. These two predictors accept new symbols at any time, without knowing the alphabet in advance. For an alphabet known in advance, a different data structure gives $O(\sigma(1+\log z/\log\log n))$ time per symbol, which is constant when $\sigma=O(1)$ and $z=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$.
papers.ko: 런-장치 BWT로 효율적인 렘플-지브 예측

papers.title: Rethinking Model Aggregation for Federated Learning with Domain Skew: A Knowledge-Preserving Perspective
papers.abs: Domain skew challenges federated learning by requiring a shared model to accommodate distinct visual distributions. Domain-specific experts can capture these distributions separately, creating an opportunity to integrate their representations in a unified predictor. We propose Federated Knowledge-Preserving Learning (FKPL), a two-stage framework that combines domain-oriented expert training with prototype-based classifier calibration. First, a one-shot subspace-based clustering procedure groups clients for intra-cluster training. The resulting expert encoders are concatenated and frozen, preserving each learned feature mapping during global integration. Second, clients interpolate their concatenated features with class-matched domain prototypes and upload the resulting virtual features. The server trains a global linear classifier on these features, concentrating classifier optimization at the server after a single feature upload. FKPL achieves average accuracies of 73.01\%, 67.00\%, and 64.51\% on Office-Caltech-10, PACS, and a four-domain subset of DomainNet, respectively. On DomainNet, its cross-domain standard deviation is 7.50 percentage points, the lowest among the evaluated methods. With the same concatenated extractor, prototype-based calibration improves average accuracy over federated classifier training by 9.99 and 14.94 percentage points on Office-Caltech-10 and PACS. These results identify classifier calibration as an effective way to combine preserved domain representations into a global predictor.
papers.ko: 도메인 스케이와 함께 연방적 학습을 위한 모형 집합을 재고: 지식 보존의 관점

papers.title: AgenticMobility: An Open-Source Platform for Multi-AI-Agent Mobility Dynamics
papers.abs: Understanding mobility dynamics and the effects of urban transportation management policies requires examining how individual travel decisions, traffic conditions, and policy interventions influence one another over time. We present AgenticMobility, an open-source experimental platform for studying how mobility AI agents and other AI agents interact, adapt through repeated experience, and collectively shape mobility outcomes. Persistent agents retain identities and relevant states across rounds, with explicit interfaces defining information access, admissible actions, and decision schedules; linked records trace decisions, execution, and feedback. In the current implementation, large language model (LLM) agents act as travelers choosing routes and departure times and as a manager periodically adjusting link charges within MATSim. A preliminary demonstration spans 100 simulated days in each of five configurations, with one run per configuration and a shared simulation seed. In the joint traveler--manager run, all 1,179,300 finalized target decisions satisfied action constraints; execution checks verified implementation of accepted choices and preservation of personal memories across days. Trajectories show stable route choices alongside departure-time adjustments and differences between controlled-trip and population-wide outcomes. The platform supports experiments on individual adaptation, collective outcomes, and management interventions by varying information access, retained experience, and management feedback. Source code is available at https://github.com/Agentic-City-Research/Agentic-Mobility

papers.title: RECEIPT: Measuring and Repairing the Return Assumption of LLM Agents in Web Service Operations
papers.abs: LLM agents operate Web infrastructure from the command line and rely on a return assumption, namely that each tool call returns within a bounded time and with its requested action finished. Many commands, however, ask a question before they act, and the agent's harness either closes the program's input or keeps it open as a terminal at which nobody types. With closed input, the program can return status 0 without the requested action. With open input, it waits until a time limit, and the agent pays in time and tokens. To the best of our knowledge, this paper is the first to measure and repair the return assumption. We collect 91,469 production tool calls and 89,047 public agent trajectories, test how 8 widely used harnesses launch commands, and build Litmus, a catalog of 158 checked command-line invocations, and Tripwire, a benchmark of 25 task pairs that differ only in whether a question guards the requested action. We then propose RECEIPT, which keeps the input open, reads what each process waits for from system calls, and returns this state to an unmodified agent through a model-checked protocol. On Litmus, closed input causes 11.5% of tested invocations to return status 0 without performing the requested action, and 7 of 8 harnesses close input when no terminal is attached. An unanswered question at a plain terminal multiplies a task's token use by 2.9, and the input connection moves an LLM from 7th to 3rd place among 8. Across 5 LLMs, RECEIPT reduces false claims of success by 73.5% and completes all 25 guarded tasks on a second harness. An agent's reliability therefore depends on what its harness lets it observe as well as on its LLM. Agent builders should report what each tool call did, not only how it ended, and benchmark maintainers should fix and report the input connection before they rank LLMs.
papers.ko: RECEIPT: 웹 서비스 운영에서 LLM 에이전트의 반환 인수 측정 및 수리

papers.title: Direct Knowledge Transfer for Offline Q-Learning
papers.abs: Data-driven sequential decision making in marketing and healthcare can benefit from observations collected in related environments, particularly when data in the environment of interest are limited. Transferring such information requires accounting for differences in rewards and transition dynamics across environments. We study knowledge transfer for offline reinforcement learning through a joint estimation framework that directly integrates source information into target value-function learning. We propose Direct Transfer Fitted Q-Iteration (DFQI), which updates the target Q-function while simultaneously borrowing the source information through an L1 penalty that links the target coefficients to a weighted aggregate of source coefficients, with both determined jointly within each Bellman update. Using sieve approximation, we establish statistical guarantees for target estimation and policy learning in stationary discounted environments with common or heterogeneous transition kernels. Empirical studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DFQI framework in transferring source information to improve policy learning with limited target data.
papers.ko: 오프라인 Q-Learning에 대한 직접 지식 전송

papers.title: Step-Zero Attack: Agent Safety Before Observability
papers.abs: Existing attacks and defenses for coding agents act once content enters the model context: injected text persuades the model, and guards inspect what the model reads. Yet to judge whether processing an unknown archive, network response, or image is safe, an agent often must process it first, and that step can do harm before any content reaches the model. We call this first processing Step Zero, and harm done by it a Step-Zero attack. Across seven harnesses and six models, each agent received only a path or URL to a crafted input, paired with a benign twin showing the same visible fields. Step Zero is where most agents are already unsafe: 32/42 harness-model pairs overran a 4 MiB disk budget, 26/42 before the model saw any member, and four of the six models did so in every round (84/84), so the damage precedes any model-side defense. Every twin stayed within budget, so the attacker's bytes alone cause the harm. On network and image inputs the risk moves to what the agent writes: agents stored the body under the name the input declared, letting the input decide what is written, and their checks faded once cues were removed. Model-free tests trace the harm to the processing primitive, so we defend it there: a gate that counts the bytes each call produces held every routed extraction within budget while agents completed 25/28 tasks. Vendors should pair such gates with safety-alignment training that teaches agents to inspect an input before processing it.
papers.ko: 무단 공격: 관찰 가능하기 전에 요원 안전

papers.title: Launder-Bench: Can Repository-Level Agentic Code Laundering Be Detected?
papers.abs: Coding agents can now rewrite repository-scale codebases while preserving tested behavior, creating a new challenge for plagiarism detection, license auditing, and software provenance. We ask whether such rewrites can still be traced to their source. Existing clone benchmarks emphasize fragments and bounded edits, while repository-transformation benchmarks evaluate functional correctness rather than provenance. Moreover, ranking the most similar source does not establish derivation when independent implementations can be similarly close. We define repository-level agentic code laundering and introduce Launder-Bench, to our knowledge the first repository-level benchmark for provenance under agentic rewriting, constructed from 282 real-world repositories. A source-hidden reconstruction protocol decomposes source behavior, reconstructs modules and repository structure, and retains rewrites only after execution-based verification. We evaluate the same provenance problem in two complementary settings: Launder-Bench-Pair contains 1,128 pairwise instances asking whether two repositories share provenance, while Launder-Bench-Attr contains 229 source-attribution instances asking which candidate is the source, with abstention when evidence is insufficient. Measured same-domain independent repositories establish how much similarity can arise without shared provenance and provide detector-specific reference bands. Existing methods remain far from saturating Launder-Bench: the strongest static method reaches only 0.66 AUROC on pairwise detection, while repository encoders rank the true source first on up to 22% of attribution queries but earn calibrated attribution credit on only 1-2%. These results reveal a systematic gap between relative code similarity and source-specific provenance evidence, providing a reproducible target for provenance detection under agentic rewriting.
papers.ko: 세탁자 벤치: 저장소 수준의 에이전틱 코드 세탁을 감지할 수 있습니까?

papers.title: Beyond Prompt Injection: The Tool Update Gap in LLM Agent Security
papers.abs: Large language model based agents increasingly rely on external tools to invoke services and interact with web resources. These tools can evolve through software updates, yet agentic frameworks may continue trusting them without re-verifying their safety after implementation changes. This tool update gap creates a supply-chain vulnerability in agentic systems: because updated tool code executes outside the LLM's context window, malicious functionality embedded in tool updates can bypass defenses centered on model-visible interactions, leaving agents exposed to stealthy, persistent threats that existing in-context defenses can hardly address. To thoroughly investigate this threat, we introduce ETUDE (Exploiting Tool Updates for Direct Execution), an attack that embeds malicious functionality into updates of initially benign tools to produce compromised tools, while preserving their legitimate tool functionality. Unlike prompt-based attacks, ETUDE operates entirely outside the LLM's context and requires no adversarial instructions, thereby bypassing defenses restricted to model-visible content. We evaluate ETUDE across three representative attack workloads and seven widely used commercial and open-source agentic frameworks, including Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and Claude Code. The results show that ETUDE achieves a 97.6% ASR while maintaining a 95.9% legitimate task completion rate. We further examine existing defenses and find that they provide insufficient protection against this threat. These findings expose a fundamental blind spot in current agent security practices: trust established for a tool does not necessarily remain valid after its implementation updates.

papers.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Glaucoma Detection CNNs: Effects of Operating Threshold, Multi-Source Training, and Color Normalization
papers.abs: Deep learning models for glaucoma detection are usually tested on images from the same dataset used for training. That says little about how they will work at a new hospital or with a new camera. We fine-tuned five ImageNet-pretrained CNNs (ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, InceptionV3) with identical settings on one of three public fundus datasets (ACRIMA, ORIGA, RIM-ONE DL). Each was tested on a held-out part of its own dataset and on the other two datasets in full. We used three random seeds and report mean and SD over seeds. Mean in-domain AUC was 0.913 and cross-source AUC was 0.702, a drop of 0.211 (SD 0.030; 95% CI 0.135 to 0.286). After correction for multiple comparisons we found no evidence that any architecture did better, though three seeds give low power. At thresholds set on the source validation data, specificity fell from 0.870 to 0.506 and sensitivity from 0.831 to 0.726. Resetting the threshold on 10% of the target images raised specificity to 0.670 but lowered sensitivity to 0.609, and balanced accuracy rose only from 0.616 to 0.639. Training on two sources together did not help (held-out AUC 0.695 versus 0.702). LAB reference normalization (cross-source AUC 0.755) and strong color augmentation (0.754) gave similar gains, cutting the drop to about 0.16. Ben Graham normalization (0.733) and CLAHE (0.712) helped less, and gray-world (0.696) did not help. The two best methods raised specificity but lowered sensitivity. On G1020, used only for testing, AUC stayed near 0.5 in every condition, and networks trained within G1020 were also close to chance. Strong in-domain results do not show that a glaucoma model will work on new data. Normalization and color augmentation reduce the drop but do not remove it. Studies should report external validation and check the operating threshold, not only AUC.

papers.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
papers.abs: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, the decomposition needs no approximation: each class's probability above its no-information share splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM) over the picture and measurable on the hardware that classifies. For the quadratic form behind each class probability it equals Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline, in closed form. Deleting the 5 % of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73 % to 9 %, as occlusion does with 1,024 extra runs per picture, whereas gradient saliency removes much less. One architecture serves both: a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at a single wavelength reach 72.3 % on Caltech-10 colour photographs (96.8 % on MNIST, 86.7 % on Fashion-MNIST, 47.9 % on colour CIFAR-10). On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask applied before approximate loading, 300 Caltech-10 test pictures were classified at 37.7 % against 10 % by chance (56.3 % in exact simulation), and 2x2 maps of ten correctly and confidently classified pictures, estimated on the chip, agreed with the exact ones (r = 0.77). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data.

papers.title: Query-efficient scan-and-search watermark localization
papers.abs: Recently, the detection of AI-generated content has been of particular importance in various fields of our society. For accountability purposes, many large language models (LLMs) have implicitly watermarked their outputs. Localizing such watermarks requires a piece of text to undergo an additional verification process. Existing localization methods typically rely on dense token-level scoring, making verification costly even when an LLM-generated watermark only sparsely appears. To tackle this problem, we design a new adaptive allocation strategy that first maintains broad document coverage and then progressively concentrates the detection budget on regions that exhibit stronger watermark evidence or are more likely to contain watermarked content. We then transform the statistical signals from the selected regions into e-values and employ the proposed token-weighted e-BH procedure to determine the localized watermark regions. The resulting framework is called BELL (Budgeted E-evidence Localization for LLM Watermarks). Theoretically, BELL can control the token-weighted false discovery rate (FDR) without independence assumptions across regions. Finally, extensive experimental results demonstrate that BELL consistently outperforms competing methods across multiple LLMs, datasets, and watermarking schemes.
papers.ko: 쿼리 효율적인 스캔 및 검색 워터마크 현지화

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in High-Energy Physics: A Survey from Accelerator Control to Theory Exploration
papers.abs: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a machine learning paradigm in which an agent learns a decision-making policy by interacting with an environment, guided by a scalar reward rather than explicit supervision. Supervised and unsupervised learning have become indispensable tools in high-energy physics (HEP), but they learn from fixed datasets, whereas many HEP tasks are closed-loop decisions: the data an algorithm observes depend on its choices, the feedback is sparse or delayed, and the objective is often measured on a real machine or in a stochastic simulation, not by a differentiable model. This survey reviews the application of RL to such tasks: accelerator control and feedback, data quality monitoring, jet grooming, clustering, and representation, charged particle tracking, beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) and string model building, detector design, trigger control, analysis, and formal quantum field theory computation. It provides a self-contained introduction to the underlying RL methods, from model-free and model-based to multi-agent, offline, inverse, and bandit approaches, reviews each domain against its traditional methods, and summarizes the head-to-head comparisons. The applications range from policies deployed on real accelerators and evaluated on recorded collision data to exploratory studies in formal theory. RL is most advantageous for repeated tasks with a fast simulator, decisions inside fast control loops, operation under faults and corrupted measurements, physics-based rewards in place of labels, and sequential discrete constructions with a reusable policy, while Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and differentiable methods remain competitive elsewhere. We conclude with the open challenges that recur across domains, including reward design, sim-to-real transfer, safety, the lack of shared benchmarks, and the statistical validity of policy-driven decisions.

papers.title: Rare Event Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Large Deviations
papers.abs: We study finite-horizon reinforcement learning with a safety constraint on the probability of reaching a failure set. In contrast to the well-studied safe reinforcement learning literature, we consider problems where the probability of reaching the failure set is vanishingly small, but the consequences of reaching the failure set are catastrophic. Direct simulation and estimation of the optimal policy is naturally ineffective when the failure probability is extremely small. Moreover, on a real system the controller can only choose actions, and this is not enough to make failures frequent. In contrast to the rare event simulation literature, our goal is not to estimate the probability of the rare event occurrence, but to upper bound it such that the failure constraint is satisfied. Thus, instead of sampling failures, we use the large deviations principle. We define a damage variable that on exceeding a certain threshold indicates failure. We study the cumulant generating function (CGF) as its positive root provides an upper bound on the failure probability via Cramer's theorem. We extend this approach to Markov decision processes with hitting times through state-action CGFs, and give finite-horizon and state-dependent versions of the bound. The state-action CGFs do not depend on the policy and can be estimated from regular transitions, so the bound can be checked for any policy a priori. This gives a policy improvement algorithm in which every policy satisfies the failure constraint with high probability.
papers.ko: 희귀 사건으로 제한된 강화 학습

papers.title: Black Hole Love Numbers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abs: We develop and validate a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for computing the tidal Love numbers of black holes directly from their perturbation equations. We consider static perturbations of the Kerr black hole, whose exact hypergeometric solutions provide a controlled benchmark for both the numerical solver and the extraction of the physical response. The framework combines exact enforcement of the horizon boundary conditions with an $H^2$-Sobolev loss that incorporates derivatives of the differential-equation residual. The Love number is then obtained by extracting the asymptotic coefficients of the learned solution, without using the analytic connection formula. Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below $10^{-5}$. Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude, while independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients. The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.

papers.title: Reduced Cost Influence Functions for Predict-then-Optimize under Noisy Data
papers.abs: Machine learning models deployed in decision-making pipelines, from vehicle routing to dynamic pricing to clinical decision support, must remain reliable in the face of low-quality training data. We study a predict-then-optimize setting in which an upstream model predicts the cost vector of a downstream linear program, with a large pool of noisy training data supplemented by a small curated set of clean data. We introduce Reduced Cost Influence Functions (RCIFs), which combine influence functions from robust statistics with the geometry of linear optimization to estimate how each training point shifts downstream decisions. Building on this, we propose a reweighting algorithm that uses RCIFs to downweight harmful training points and reduce downstream regret. Experiments on random linear programs and shortest-path problems show that our approach reduces regret, and accompanying theory characterizes properties of RCIFs and identifies regimes favorable to our method relative to baselines.
